title: Linux disk full caused by logs or journal growth

checks.purpose: separate block exhaustion from inode exhaustion
locate large directories without crossing filesystems
measure journal usage
find deleted files still held open

remediation.action: fix logrotate policy, then rotate affected application logs
journalctl --rotate followed by approved --vacuum-size or --vacuum-time limit
restart only process holding a confirmed deleted large file

rollback: restart affected logger/application if rotation handoff fails
verify: log growth rate returns to baseline
safety: never delete unknown files by size alone
journal vacuum removes archived journals only
record reclaimed bytes and affected service
source: Blackout Ops curated runbook; systemd journalctl official behavior

title: Linux filesystem inode exhaustion
symptoms: No space left despite free GiB

checks.purpose: confirm inode exhaustion
count files only inside approved path
preview stale deletion candidates

remediation.action: delete only previewed stale files covered by retention policy
add bounded retention or queue consumer fix

rollback: restore deleted files from snapshot/backup when required
safety: approved-path must be explicit
no recursive delete against root, home, workspace, or unresolved variable

title: Kubernetes node DiskPressure

checks.purpose: confirm DiskPressure condition, taint, capacity and eviction events
locate eviction and garbage-collection evidence
inspect runtime images and stopped containers on affected node
identify nodefs/imagefs/containerfs or inode pressure

remediation.action: allow kubelet garbage collection to reclaim dead containers and unused images; correct kubelet GC thresholds if misconfigured
fix workload ephemeral-storage requests/limits or runaway log source
manually remove only confirmed unused runtime artifacts when kubelet cannot recover

safety: do not use external garbage collection that can conflict with kubelet
do not manually remove active container layers
source: Kubernetes node-pressure eviction and garbage-collection documentation

title: CrashLoopBackOff caused by OOMKilled or low memory limit

checks.purpose: confirm OOMKilled, exit code and time
read previous crashed container log
inspect limits, events and node pressure
compare observed memory with request and limit when metrics are available

remediation.action: raise memory request/limit only after measured requirement and capacity check
roll back release when memory regression began with current revision
fix memory leak or reduce startup concurrency

rollback: restore previous resource requests and limits
safety: do not raise limits beyond node capacity
check blast radius before rollout
source: Kubernetes pod debugging documentation plus P0 case labels

title: CrashLoopBackOff caused by invalid command, args, or image

checks.purpose: capture startup error
inspect resolved image, command and args
compare failing revision with last healthy revision

remediation.action: correct image, command or args in source manifest and apply reviewed change
roll back to last healthy Deployment revision for rapid recovery

safety: record current revision before change
never substitute an unverified mutable image tag
source: Kubernetes pod debugging documentation; ITBench Scenario-105 pattern

title: CrashLoopBackOff caused by missing or invalid ConfigMap/Secret

checks.purpose: find missing object/key events
confirm referenced object exists without exposing secret data
inspect references and key names

remediation.action: restore expected ConfigMap/Secret from approved source or correct reference
restart rollout after configuration is restored

rollback: restore previous object version from secret manager/config repository
safety: never place secret values in RAG, logs, prompts or audit output
compare names and hashes, not plaintext secret content
source: Blackout Ops curated runbook plus P0 case labels

title: CrashLoopBackOff caused by unavailable dependency

checks.purpose: identify dependency host, port and failure
confirm dependency service and ready endpoints
identify policy that may block traffic

remediation.action: restore dependency or correct endpoint/port configuration
add bounded retry/backoff or startup probe so transient dependency delay does not crash process

rollback: restore previous endpoint, environment variable or NetworkPolicy
safety: do not delete NetworkPolicy as a diagnostic shortcut
validate least-privilege connectivity
source: Blackout Ops curated runbook plus P0 case labels

title: Container restart caused by liveness or startup probe misconfiguration

checks.purpose: confirm probe failure events
inspect probe protocol, port, path and timing
separate probe kill from application crash

remediation.action: correct probe endpoint/port/protocol
add startupProbe or tune timing from measured startup behavior

safety: do not remove health probes permanently
avoid masking real application failure with excessive thresholds

title: Kubernetes DNS failure from wrong Service name or namespace
symptoms: short name works only in one namespace

checks.purpose: test fully qualified service name from affected namespace
confirm exact Service name and namespace
inspect search domains and nameserver

remediation.action: correct Service FQDN, namespace or application environment variable
roll out corrected workload configuration

verify: DNS error rate returns to baseline
safety: verify from affected namespace
do not change cluster-wide DNS before proving cluster-wide impact

title: Cluster-wide DNS failure in CoreDNS
root_causes: Corefile forwarding loop or bad upstream

checks.purpose: check DNS pod health
confirm DNS Service and ClusterIP
confirm ready DNS endpoints
inspect query and forwarding errors

remediation.action: restore reviewed CoreDNS ConfigMap/Corefile or upstream resolver
restart CoreDNS Deployment after configuration correction

safety: cluster-wide blast radius
capture Corefile and current rollout revision before change

title: Service resolves but has no ready endpoints

checks.purpose: inspect selector, port and targetPort
inspect endpoint readiness and ports
compare pod labels with Service selector

remediation.action: correct Service selector, port, targetPort or protocol
repair backing pod readiness failure when selector is correct

safety: distinguish DNS resolution from Service routing
preview selector matches before applying
source: Kubernetes Service and DNS diagnostic practice; Cloud-OpsBench routing patterns

title: Pod startup failure from image registry DNS resolution
root_causes: proxy or egress DNS path broken

checks.purpose: capture exact image pull and DNS event
test registry DNS from affected node context
inspect affected node resolver configuration

remediation.action: correct registry hostname or node resolver/upstream DNS configuration
retry rollout after DNS path is restored

safety: do not bypass TLS or switch to an untrusted registry
do not expose registry credentials in diagnostics

title: Linux systemd service restart loop or failed unit

checks.purpose: capture unit state, exit status and recent messages
read complete failure sequence

checks.command: systemctl show <unit> -p FragmentPath -p ExecMainStatus -p NRestarts -p Restart
checks.purpose: inspect loaded unit, exit status and restart behavior
validate unit syntax without starting service

remediation.action: correct reviewed unit, environment, permissions or dependency configuration, then run systemctl daemon-reload
restart only the affected unit after configuration validation

rollback: restore previous unit or environment file
verify: journal has no new startup error
safety: capture FragmentPath and current file before editing
do not disable Restart policy to hide an unresolved crash

title: Linux process killed by kernel or systemd OOM policy

checks.purpose: confirm kernel OOM victim and timestamp

checks.command: systemctl show <unit> -p MemoryCurrent -p MemoryMax -p MemoryHigh -p OOMPolicy
checks.purpose: inspect systemd cgroup memory policy
measure host pressure and top consumers

remediation.action: fix application leak or bound concurrency; deploy reviewed change
adjust MemoryHigh or MemoryMax only after capacity and blast-radius checks
restart only the confirmed affected service after pressure is controlled

safety: do not disable memory controls globally
do not raise limits beyond physical capacity

title: Linux host DNS resolver failure

checks.purpose: test resolution through libc/NSS used by applications
inspect link-specific DNS and query result when systemd-resolved is used
inspect resolver ownership, nameservers and search domains
separate DNS protocol failure from application behavior

remediation.action: restore reviewed NetworkManager or systemd-resolved DNS configuration
restart the active resolver service after configuration validation
change firewall or routing rules only after proving DNS packets are blocked

verify: getent and resolvectl resolve expected address
safety: do not overwrite a managed resolv.conf symlink blindly
test internal and external zones separately
preserve air-gapped resolver policy

title: Linux TLS service certificate expired or not yet valid

checks.purpose: rule out incorrect system time
capture served chain and verification result
inspect local certificate identity and validity
inspect renewal scheduling without changing state

remediation.action: renew or restore the approved certificate chain through the configured CA/ACME workflow
validate service configuration, then reload only the affected TLS service

rollback: restore previous certificate and key files from protected backup
reload the prior known-good service configuration
verify: served certificate serial matches intended deployment
validity window includes current UTC time
safety: never print or copy private keys into logs or prompts
do not disable TLS verification
treat certificate replacement as a scoped write action

title: Linux service connection refused or expected port not listening

checks.purpose: identify listening address, port and owning process
inspect service state and exit status
capture bind or startup error
test exact address and port from approved network context

remediation.action: correct reviewed bind address or port configuration and restart only affected service
change firewall policy only after listener and path are proven healthy and the required flow is approved

verify: local and approved remote health checks pass
safety: do not expose service on 0.0.0.0 without requirement
do not flush firewall rules
record affected interface and blast radius
